newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end lower, electricity sector gloomy.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end lower, electricity sector gloomy.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed almost one percent lower on Tuesday as the government's announcement of measures to cut power consumption brought further declines in electricity shares, traders said.
The slide is seen resuming at the opening with investors gloomy about the outlook for the power sector, they said.
"The market is entering a phase of adjustment. The IPSA index could fall back down to 113-114 points," one dealer said.
The 40-share index ended down 0.93 percent at 116.06 points. The general index shed 0.34 percent to 5,322.29 points.
Turnover shrank slightly to 12.5 billion pesos from 12.8 billion pesos Monday.
Electricity shares ended sharply lower on fears that the government's decision to cut power voltage in central Chile by five percent will cut into company profits, said dealers.
The measures were taken as this year's drought has slashed power output from electricity generators.
"If the measures continue for the next couple of months, then they will hit operating earnings," said one dealer.
Endesa tumbled 3.14 percent to 247 pesos, while Enersis was off 2.15 percent at 250-1/2 pesos.
Winners included bottler Andina which climbed on news the company will invest up to $1 billion in the next two years in Latin America, said dealers.
Andina ended up 2.66 percent at 1,350 pesos.
